bull_bear.body:
- scale: dominant share of the CV parabolic-spring category — evidence: parabolic springs are approximately 30% of CV spring demand and JAI holds approximately 85% market share in this category (MD&A); new Adityapur parabolic capacity became operational in FY2025-26 — against it: the company's own risk section says its business depends on the cyclical commercial vehicle segment
- distribution: pan-India CV suspension aftermarket channel — evidence: 350+ distributors, 20,000+ retailers and 25,000+ mechanics enrolled in a loyalty programme; 29 authorised service centres and ~20 certified workshops for trailer suspension — against it: new markets (Aftermarket India + exports) were still only approximately 22% of consolidated revenue in FY2025-26 against the 40% target
- technology: licensed and absorbed suspension technology plus own IP — evidence: tapered leaf spring technology from NHK Spring (Japan) and air suspension/lift axle technology from Ridewell (USA) fully absorbed; two patents owned (air suspension) and a third applied for; 140+ copyrighted product designs — against it: Tinsley Bridge (UK) extralite spring and special steel technology is only partially absorbed
- customer lock-in: plants co-located with OEM assembly hubs and multi-product supply to the same OEMs — evidence: plant map pairs each plant with named OEM plants (e.g. Jamshedpur/Adityapur with Tata Motors, Hosur with Volvo/Ashok Leyland/Scania); stabilizer bar supply extended from Tata Motors to Mahindra & Mahindra and slipper suspension supply started to Ashok Leyland in FY2025-26
- integration: in-house axle and rubber components for trailer suspension systems — evidence: the axle is approximately 60% of a trailer suspension system's value and an integrated suspension plant with in-house axle manufacturing at Indore plus a rubber components facility at Malanpur are board-approved and in execution [planned]
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on the cyclical commercial-vehicle segment — The Risk Management section says a key aim of Lakshya RISE 5000 is to diversify products and geographies to reduce dependence on the cyclical CV segment. New markets (aftermarket + exports) were only about 22% of consolidated revenue in FY2025-26, against a 40% target, so OEM CV demand still dominates.
- Input and logistics cost shocks from the Gulf conflict — The MD&A says the Gulf conflict and the Strait of Hormuz disruption created near-term headwinds on energy, steel and maritime logistics costs. Management says it is containing them through disciplined sourcing and supply-chain coordination.
- Cybersecurity / IT disruption — The company suffered a ransomware incident in FY2024-25. Since then it has hardened its defences with PKF Algosmic as Cyber Controls Implementation Partner and completed RAMCO ERP integration across all group locations.
- Ramp-up of newly commissioned subsidiaries — The statutory auditor made the carrying value of investments in Jai Suspensions Limited and Jai Automotive Components Limited a Key Audit Matter: their net worth is below the Company's investment because of losses in the project-implementation phase. The Board expects both to ramp up now that commercial production has started.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Jamna Auto Industries (JAI) makes automotive suspension products for commercial vehicles — tapered, parabolic and hybrid leaf springs, lift axles, trailer and air suspension systems, stabilizer bars, slipper suspensions, drop axles and allied components. It supplies India's CV OEMs from plants sited near their assembly hubs, and is building an aftermarket business (distributors, retailers, mechanics) and an export business under its Lakshya RISE 5000 roadmap. It is positioning itself to move from component manufacturer to integrated suspension-system provider.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Leaf springs:** Conventional / tapered leaf spring, Parabolic leaf spring, Hybrid leaf spring assembly, Z-spring, BS VI-compliant springs
- **Suspension systems & axles:** Lift axle, Trailer mechanical suspension, Trailer air suspension, Trailer mechanical and air suspension with lift axle, Bus air suspension, Slipper suspension, Stabilizer bar, Drop axle, Trailer axle
- **Allied / aftermarket components:** U-bolts, Spring allied components, Trailer allied components, Lift axle allied components, Brake linings, Clutches, Water pumps, Bearings, Jack rods, Universal joint crosses
business.title: Products & brands

- Jai Suspensions Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) subsidiary since 31/08/2016; supplies semi-finished and finished goods to the Company and buys raw materials procured on its behalf; also sells property, plant and equipment to the Company.

outlook.body:
- Lakshya RISE 5000: a five-year roadmap built on market diversification (Indian aftermarket and exports) and product diversification, aimed at reducing dependence on the cyclical commercial-vehicle segment.
- Aftermarket India push: deepen the distributor/retailer/mechanic channel (350+ distributors, 20,000+ retailers, 25,000+ mechanics), grow allied (non-spring) products in the aftermarket mix, and support it with supply-chain focus (Yamuna Nagar dedicated to aftermarket, small-batch line) and digitalisation (DMS, RAMCO ERP, mechanic loyalty programme).
- Export build-out: expand the international distributor network and broaden the export range from leaf springs to parabolic springs and allied products, with the Hosur plant dedicated to export production.
- Move up the value chain from component maker to integrated suspension-system provider: in-house axle manufacturing (axle is ~60% of a trailer suspension system's value) at an integrated Indore plant, plus in-house rubber components (bushes, bolsters).
- Raise content per vehicle with OEMs by adding products beyond springs — stabiliser bars, slipper suspensions, drop axles and lift axles — to existing OEM relationships.
- Build a dedicated nationwide after-sales service organisation for trailer suspension (authorised service centres, certified workshops, training centres, digital customer care system).
- Add parabolic spring capacity to serve the OEM shift from conventional leaf springs to parabolic springs (Adityapur operational; Pithampur planned).
- Fund all capex from internal accruals with no reliance on external debt, while moving dividend payout toward 50%.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY2025-26 brought two new plants on stream through subsidiaries: Jai Suspensions Limited started commercial production at its parabolic leaf spring plant at Adityapur, Jharkhand, and Jai Automotive Components Limited started U-bolt and leaf spring production at Indore, Madhya Pradesh. U-bolt output from Indore is also being sold through Aftermarket India. Further projects are board-approved and in execution. The chairman describes a new parabolic spring facility at Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh (Rs 170 crore, 21,600 MT, commissioning targeted by March 2028); the MD&A project list separately names a parabolic leaf spring project at Indore. The MD&A also lists an integrated suspension system plant at Indore with in-house axle manufacturing (the axle is about 60% of a trailer suspension system's value) and an in-house rubber components facility at Malanpur for bushes, bolsters and allied parts. The chairman states the company invested Rs 257 crore in capex during the year for capacity expansion, modernisation and product expansion, against Rs 196 crore the year before. The MD&A says all capex is funded through internal accruals without external debt. On the service side, the company plans more trailer-suspension training centres beyond Pillaipakkam.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian CV production reached a record ~11.75 lakh units in FY2025-26 (~13% growth), driven by the GST 2.0 reforms of September 2025 and sustained government infrastructure spending.
- OEMs are accelerating the transition from conventional leaf springs to parabolic springs, which are now ~30% of CV spring demand; JAI holds ~85% share of that category.
- Rising adoption of advanced commercial vehicles is accelerating demand for technology-based suspension components; hybrid and BS VI-compliant springs are aligned with evolving regulations and OEM requirements.
- Air suspension systems, lift axles and allied products are gaining traction; management expects the suspension systems market to grow significantly over the next five years.
- Aftermarket India grew ~14% in FY2025-26 (highest ever for a second consecutive year) and allied products' share of the aftermarket mix is rising (3% to 6% to 8% over three years).
- New products contributed approximately 47% of revenue in FY2025-26.
- Gulf conflict / Strait of Hormuz disruption created near-term headwinds on energy, steel and maritime logistics costs, managed through sourcing discipline without material disruption.
- Management attributes the year's improvement to the broad-based CV industry recovery, operating leverage and cost discipline.
- Further OEM additions for stabiliser bars are under discussion, after supplies were extended from Tata Motors to Mahindra & Mahindra.

- Aftermarket India grew ~14% in FY2025-26 (highest ever for a second consecutive year) and allied products' share of the aftermarket mix is rising (3% to 6% to 8% over three years).
- New products contributed approximately 47% of revenue in FY2025-26.
- Gulf conflict / Strait of Hormuz disruption created near-term headwinds on energy, steel and maritime logistics costs, managed through sourcing discipline without material disruption.
- Management attributes the year's improvement to the broad-based CV industry recovery, operating leverage and cost discipline.
- Further OEM additions for stabiliser bars are under discussion, after supplies were extended from Tata Motors to Mahindra & Mahindra.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Lakshya RISE 5000: a five-year roadmap built on market diversification (Indian aftermarket and exports) and product diversification, aimed at reducing dependence on the cyclical commercial-vehicle segment.
- Aftermarket India push: deepen the distributor/retailer/mechanic channel (350+ distributors, 20,000+ retailers, 25,000+ mechanics), grow allied (non-spring) products in the aftermarket mix, and support it with supply-chain focus (Yamuna Nagar dedicated to aftermarket, small-batch line) and digitalisation (DMS, RAMCO ERP, mechanic loyalty programme).
- Export build-out: expand the international distributor network and broaden the export range from leaf springs to parabolic springs and allied products, with the Hosur plant dedicated to export production.
- Move up the value chain from component maker to integrated suspension-system provider: in-house axle manufacturing (axle is ~60% of a trailer suspension system's value) at an integrated Indore plant, plus in-house rubber components (bushes, bolsters).
- Raise content per vehicle with OEMs by adding products beyond springs — stabiliser bars, slipper suspensions, drop axles and lift axles — to existing OEM relationships.
- Build a dedicated nationwide after-sales service organisation for trailer suspension (authorised service centres, certified workshops, training centres, digital customer care system).
- Add parabolic spring capacity to serve the OEM shift from conventional leaf springs to parabolic springs (Adityapur operational; Pithampur planned).
- Fund all capex from internal accruals with no reliance on external debt, while moving dividend payout toward 50%.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY2025-26 brought two new plants on stream through subsidiaries: Jai Suspensions Limited started commercial production at its parabolic leaf spring plant at Adityapur, Jharkhand, and Jai Automotive Components Limited started U-bolt and leaf spring production at Indore, Madhya Pradesh. U-bolt output from Indore is also being sold through Aftermarket India. Further projects are board-approved and in execution. The chairman describes a new parabolic spring facility at Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh (Rs 170 crore, 21,600 MT, commissioning targeted by March 2028); the MD&A project list separately names a parabolic leaf spring project at Indore. The MD&A also lists an integrated suspension system plant at Indore with in-house axle manufacturing (the axle is about 60% of a trailer suspension system's value) and an in-house rubber components facility at Malanpur for bushes, bolsters and allied parts. The chairman states the company invested Rs 257 crore in capex during the year for capacity expansion, modernisation and product expansion, against Rs 196 crore the year before. The MD&A says all capex is funded through internal accruals without external debt. On the service side, the company plans more trailer-suspension training centres beyond Pillaipakkam.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- scale: dominant share of the CV parabolic-spring category — evidence: parabolic springs are approximately 30% of CV spring demand and JAI holds approximately 85% market share in this category (MD&A); new Adityapur parabolic capacity became operational in FY2025-26 — against it: the company's own risk section says its business depends on the cyclical commercial vehicle segment
- distribution: pan-India CV suspension aftermarket channel — evidence: 350+ distributors, 20,000+ retailers and 25,000+ mechanics enrolled in a loyalty programme; 29 authorised service centres and ~20 certified workshops for trailer suspension — against it: new markets (Aftermarket India + exports) were still only approximately 22% of consolidated revenue in FY2025-26 against the 40% target
- technology: licensed and absorbed suspension technology plus own IP — evidence: tapered leaf spring technology from NHK Spring (Japan) and air suspension/lift axle technology from Ridewell (USA) fully absorbed; two patents owned (air suspension) and a third applied for; 140+ copyrighted product designs — against it: Tinsley Bridge (UK) extralite spring and special steel technology is only partially absorbed
- customer lock-in: plants co-located with OEM assembly hubs and multi-product supply to the same OEMs — evidence: plant map pairs each plant with named OEM plants (e.g. Jamshedpur/Adityapur with Tata Motors, Hosur with Volvo/Ashok Leyland/Scania); stabilizer bar supply extended from Tata Motors to Mahindra & Mahindra and slipper suspension supply started to Ashok Leyland in FY2025-26
- integration: in-house axle and rubber components for trailer suspension systems — evidence: the axle is approximately 60% of a trailer suspension system's value and an integrated suspension plant with in-house axle manufacturing at Indore plus a rubber components facility at Malanpur are board-approved and in execution [planned]

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Dependence on the cyclical commercial-vehicle segment — The Risk Management section says a key aim of Lakshya RISE 5000 is to diversify products and geographies to reduce dependence on the cyclical CV segment. New markets (aftermarket + exports) were only about 22% of consolidated revenue in FY2025-26, against a 40% target, so OEM CV demand still dominates.
- Input and logistics cost shocks from the Gulf conflict — The MD&A says the Gulf conflict and the Strait of Hormuz disruption created near-term headwinds on energy, steel and maritime logistics costs. Management says it is containing them through disciplined sourcing and supply-chain coordination.
- Cybersecurity / IT disruption — The company suffered a ransomware incident in FY2024-25. Since then it has hardened its defences with PKF Algosmic as Cyber Controls Implementation Partner and completed RAMCO ERP integration across all group locations.
- Ramp-up of newly commissioned subsidiaries — The statutory auditor made the carrying value of investments in Jai Suspensions Limited and Jai Automotive Components Limited a Key Audit Matter: their net worth is below the Company's investment because of losses in the project-implementation phase. The Board expects both to ramp up now that commercial production has started.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

hero.oneLiner: India's commercial-vehicle suspension specialist, holding an approximately 85% share of the CV parabolic-spring category, now extending from springs into integrated trailer and air suspension systems.
